facts.title: An idea rooted in a real tutoring job
facts.text: Bong Joon Ho had tutored the son of a wealthy Seoul family in his early twenties. He considered turning that experience into a stage production.
evidence_markers: tutor for the son of a wealthy family in Seoul
stage production

facts.title: How the subtitles found ram-don
facts.text: Subtitle translator Darcy Paquet rendered the noodle dish jjapaguri as ram-don, combining ramen and udon for English-speaking viewers.
evidence_markers: Paquet rendered jjapaguri
ramen-udon

facts.title: A mansion built for the camera
facts.text: The Parks’ house was a specially constructed set. Its ground floor and garden stood on an outdoor lot, while the basement and first floor were built on set.
evidence_markers: Parks' house was a specially constructed set
empty outdoor lot

facts.title: An older tool behind the edit
facts.text: Editor Yang Jin-mo cut Parasite in Final Cut Pro 7, software that had not been updated since 2011.
evidence_markers: Yang edited the film using Final Cut Pro 7

facts.title: A familiar voice in the end credits
facts.text: Bong wrote the end-credit song Soju han jan. Choi Woo-shik, who plays Ki-woo, performed it.
evidence_markers: written by Bong and performed by Choi Woo-shik
end credits
